title: Time-delay estimation on a river
summary: Two river gauges as two noisy copies of one travelling signal: the dam's release schedule, the wave that carries it, and the cross-correlation that measures its delay.

concepts.label: Discharge
concepts.description: Volume of water passing a gauge per second (m³/s).

facts.text: USGS publishes 15-minute discharge for its stream gauges through the Water Data OGC API.

children.label: Stream gauge
children.description: A measuring station: Lees Ferry (09380000) and near Grand Canyon (09402500).

children.label: Hydropeaking
children.description: Daily release swings from a hydropower dam following electricity demand.

children.label: Tributary inflow
children.description: Water added between the gauges (Paria, Little Colorado), measured at their own gauges.

concepts.label: Flood wave
concepts.description: The travelling change in flow, which moves at its celerity rather than at the water's speed.

children.label: Travel time
children.description: Delay of the pulse between gauges.

children.label: Wave attenuation
children.description: How much the daily swing shrinks downstream.

children.label: Water velocity
children.description: Mean speed of the water itself, from USGS field measurements; slower than the wave.

concepts.label: Cross-correlation
concepts.description: Correlation of one signal with another shifted by a lag.

children.label: Delay ambiguity
children.description: A periodic signal fixes a delay only modulo its period: near-equal peaks one period apart.

children.label: Whitening
children.description: Correlating changes instead of levels to sharpen the peak.
